TiptapTextBlock.description: Primary text component - USE MULTIPLE BLOCKS for data hierarchy!
TiptapTextBlock.data_display_technique: Split stats into 2-3 blocks: huge number (200-300pt) + label (72-96pt) + context (48pt)

critical_rules.texts: Tiptap document structure OR legacy array format. For lists, use proper Tiptap doc structure with bulletList/orderedList.
critical_rules.height: Calculate as fontSize x 1.15 for single line, fontSize x 1.5 x numItems for lists
critical_rules.multiple_blocks: CRITICAL: BREAK content into MULTIPLE TiptapTextBlock components - DON'T cram everything into one!
critical_rules.lists: Use proper Tiptap structure: {type: 'doc', content: [{type: 'bulletList/orderedList', content: [listItems]}]} - NEVER manual bullets with '• '

alignment_rules.title_slides: ALWAYS use alignment='left', verticalAlignment='top' for title/cover slides
alignment_rules.content_slides: Use alignment='left' for body text, 'center' for stats/callouts, 'right' for captions
alignment_rules.vertical: Use verticalAlignment='top' for titles, 'middle' for centered content, 'bottom' for footers
alignment_rules.default: When in doubt, use alignment='left', verticalAlignment='top'

best_practices: BREAK content into multiple TiptapTextBlock components - separate blocks for title, subtitle, each bullet point
USE highlighting extensively with theme colors: {{primary}}15, {{secondary}}20, {{accent}}15-25
EMPHASIZE key numbers/terms: combine bold + textColor + highlight + backgroundColor
MIX fonts in same slide: heroFont for titles, bodyFont for content
BUCKET horizontally or vertically when 2-5 items (don't just stack!)
USE LISTS SPARINGLY: Only for 3-7 truly list-like items - prefer CustomComponents for stats/metrics
VARIETY IS KEY: Don't make every slide a bullet list - use cards, paragraphs, and visual components
Combine multiple styles in texts array for rich formatting
Use for tables with small fonts (8pt+)

text_styling.bold: Make text bold - use for emphasis
text_styling.italic: Italicize text - use for subtle emphasis or quotes

highlighting.usage: USE highlighting extensively! Make key numbers and terms pop with theme-colored highlights

font_mixing.title_font: Set fontFamily: "{{heroFont}}" for titles and emphasis
font_mixing.body_font: Set fontFamily: "{{bodyFont}}" for content and supporting text
font_mixing.strategy: Use different fonts in same slide - heroFont for headers, bodyFont for bullets

special_formatting.superscript: For TM, R, superscript numbers, footnotes

lists.bullet_list: Use {type: 'bulletList'} for unordered lists with bullets (•)
lists.structure: Each list contains listItem objects, each listItem contains a paragraph with text objects
lists.NEVER_USE: NEVER use manual bullets like '• ' with \n - always use proper bulletList/orderedList structure
lists.use_orderedList_for: Sequential steps/instructions, process workflows, rankings/priorities, chronological timeline events - anything where ORDER MATTERS
lists.use_bulletList_for: Unordered features/benefits, characteristics, multiple points where order doesn't matter, examples/options
lists.when_to_use: Use lists ONLY for 3-7 truly list-like items with short, parallel structure
lists.when_NOT_to_use: DON'T use for: single statements, stats/metrics (use CustomComponent), comparisons (use cards), body text (use paragraph)

layout_strategies.when_to_use: When you have 2-5 items with minimal text - DON'T just stack vertically!

horizontal_buckets.example: Left section at x=120, right section at x=1000, both centered

vertical_sections.example: Section 1 at y=200, section 2 at y=450, section 3 at y=700

rich_formatting_example.description: USE RICH TEXT FORMATTING - bold, highlight, and accent colors for impact

bullet_with_emphasis.description: Bullet point with key numbers/words emphasized

proper_bullet_list.description: CORRECT way to create bullet lists - use Tiptap structure

proper_numbered_list.description: CORRECT way to create numbered lists - use orderedList

horizontal_bucket_example.description: Two stats side-by-side instead of stacked

multiple_blocks_structured.description: Break NASA budget example into multiple well-formatted blocks

positioning_rules.always: Left or right half, never center

color_rules.CRITICAL: NEVER use {{background}} color for chart data (bars, lines, pie slices, points) - it will be INVISIBLE!
color_rules.background_only_for: Only use {{background}} for chart backgroundColor property (the chart's background, not the data)

CustomComponent.description: POWERFUL component for creating infographics, data visualizations, and interactive elements - USE FREQUENTLY IN PRESENTATION MODE!

capabilities.structured_layouts: Create cards, grids, comparisons when content doesn't need axis-based visualization
capabilities.hierarchies_and_flows: Build org structures, decision trees, process flows with decision_tree
capabilities.time_and_events: Show event sequences, roadmaps, milestones with interactive_timeline
capabilities.metrics_display: Present numbers with hero_stat_card, kpi_cards, animated_progress_rings
capabilities.comparisons: Show before/after, feature toggles with comparison_bars, two_card_comparison
capabilities.visual_appeal: Add modern aesthetics with morphing_blob, floating_icons, countdown_timer

CustomComponent.when_to_use: When content needs structured layout, qualitative relationships, or interactions rather than numerical axis comparison

presentation_mode_priority.philosophy: In PRESENTATION MODE, prefer CustomComponents over plain text - make it VISUAL!
presentation_mode_priority.card_layouts: Use card-based components (three_card_grid, two_card_comparison, hero_stat_card) for 70% of content slides
presentation_mode_priority.minimal_content: When you have 1-3 points, ALWAYS use a card component instead of bullet lists
presentation_mode_priority.visual_hierarchy: Cards create better visual hierarchy than text blocks
presentation_mode_priority.engagement: Animated cards are more engaging than static text

critical_rules.mandatory_format: MUST use React.createElement ONLY - NO HTML strings! This avoids ALL quote and escaping issues
critical_rules.signature: function render({ props, state, updateState, id, isThumbnail }) { - Clean signature, NO code inside destructuring!
critical_rules.variable_extraction: Extract ALL props ONCE at top: var c1 = props.primaryColor; var tc = props.textColor; NEVER redeclare variables!
critical_rules.style_format: Use JavaScript style objects with camelCase: { fontSize: '96px', fontWeight: '800', backgroundColor: '#FFF' }
critical_rules.root_sizing: Root element style MUST include: { width: '100%', height: '100%', boxSizing: 'border-box', overflow: 'hidden' }
critical_rules.children: For multiple elements, build children array and pass to parent: React.createElement('div', {style}, children)
critical_rules.no_jsx: Use React.createElement(type, props, children) - NEVER use JSX syntax
critical_rules.theme_props: ALWAYS use props.primaryColor, props.secondaryColor, props.textColor, props.fontFamily
critical_rules.state_updates: Do not call updateState during render; only in handlers/timeouts
critical_rules.completion: MUST end with complete balanced braces

fit_and_responsiveness.container: Style object should include: { overflowWrap: 'anywhere', wordBreak: 'break-word', overflow: 'hidden' }
fit_and_responsiveness.text: Use fontSize in pixels based on content length - longer text needs smaller fontSize
fit_and_responsiveness.grids: Calculate grid: totalWidth = itemWidth * cols + gap * (cols - 1); ensure it fits within width
fit_and_responsiveness.thumbnails: Skip heavy animations when isThumbnail is true
fit_and_responsiveness.padding: Declare padding ONCE: var padding = 24; (DO NOT redeclare later!)

data_visualization_priority.single_metric: Use hero_metric_showcase or hero_stat_display for maximum impact
data_visualization_priority.multiple_metrics: Use multi_stat_dashboard or kpi_cards with size hierarchy
data_visualization_priority.trends: Combine small line chart with HUGE current value display

recommended_components: three_card_grid - BEST for 2-3 stats in presentation mode (horizontal cards with big numbers)
hero_stat_card - BEST for single metric showcase (one massive number in beautiful card)
two_card_comparison - BEST for before/after or comparison (dramatic side-by-side cards)
funnel_viz - for conversion funnels and pipelines
avoid: Overly complex logic that could break

Lines.description: Multi-line component for diagrams, connections, and dividers - USES COORDINATES, NOT POSITION/WIDTH!

critical_rules.coordinates: Lines use startPoint {x, y} and endPoint {x, y} - NOT position/width/height!
critical_rules.startPoint: Object with x and y coordinates: {x: 100, y: 200}
critical_rules.endPoint: Object with x and y coordinates: {x: 300, y: 400}

best_practices: Use for dividers BELOW headers (horizontal lines)
Use for timelines and process flows
DO NOT use position/width/height - Lines don't work that way!
For horizontal divider: startPoint {x: 80, y: 200}, endPoint {x: 1840, y: 200}
For vertical divider: startPoint {x: 960, y: 100}, endPoint {x: 960, y: 980}
For arrows: set endShape: 'arrow' and connectionType: 'straight' or 'curved'

Background.description: Slide background - first component (95% should use gradient)
Background.CRITICAL_FORMAT: NEVER use gradientStartColor, gradientEndColor, gradientDirection - use gradient object

gradient.when_to_use: DEFAULT CHOICE - 95% of slides should use gradients for visual appeal and professionalism
gradient.MANDATORY_STRUCTURE: Must have 'gradient' object with 'type', 'angle', and 'stops' array

WRONG_FORMAT.WHY: This is LEGACY format and will be REJECTED

color.when_to_use: RARE - Only 5% of slides when specific minimalist design is required
best_for: Rare cases where gradient would interfere

Background.design_guidance: ALWAYS default to gradients - they add depth, sophistication and visual appeal. Only use solid colors when absolutely necessary.
